solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Attempt to protect old politician

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the attempt wraps round the old letter

parts.note: an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Someone tries to shield a veteran statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a Tory is a member of the Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a Conservative Party member in Britain, hence a kind of politician.

clue.text: Test entered by the French chartered accountant — something to watch

indicators.note: entered by means the test word has other letters going into it

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An exam is sat by a French accountant, someone to keep an eye on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered by' puts LECA inside TEST after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A telecast is a television broadcast, a programme people view.

clue.text: Writing up moor? Yes, primarily spacious

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing up means the word moor is written bottom to top, so reversed
primarily takes the first letter of yes

explanation.surface: Writing about the moor? Yes, it is vast and open.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means having plenty of space inside.

clue.text: She is out travelling — mind her property?

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of she is out moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: While she is away on a trip, would you look after her home?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: minding a particular woman's home while she is away.
explanation.definitionFit: To house-sit is to live in and look after someone's home while the owner is away.

clue.text: Regional power's time apt no more, broken up

indicators.note: broken up means the letters of time apt no more are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A great power's moment of suitability has passed, and it has collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman Empire was a Turkish-ruled state dominating the eastern Mediterranean and Middle East for centuries.

clue.text: Black fur

definitions.meaning: in heraldry and poetry ... is the colour black
the pelt of the ..., a small marten-like animal, is a prized fur

explanation.surface: A dark-coloured pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is both the heraldic word for black and the valuable fur of a northern mammal.

clue.text: Device for fastening paper, basic? Right

parts.note: a staple food or item is a basic one

explanation.surface: Is a paper-fastening gadget basic? Correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A stapler drives wire staples through sheets to hold them together.

clue.text: Fuss describing list

definitions.meaning: a commotion or bother, as in what a palaver
a list of jobs still to be done is named by these letters

explanation.surface: A commotion over what a list says.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss, and a to-do list is the chores still waiting.

clue.text: Have leading role to execute

definitions.meaning: to be the head of something is to take the leading role
to put to death, here by cutting off the head

explanation.surface: Take the top part so as to put someone to death.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as BE HEAD, the first definition is to be the head; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheading is a form of execution by cutting off the head.

clue.text: Most imprecise, loses time, digesting nothing

indicators.note: digesting means taking something inside, so the zero goes within the other letters

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone sloppy keeps losing track of time while eating nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digesting' puts O inside LOSEST, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose here means vague or inexact, so the superlative is the least precise.

clue.text: Musicians getting round resistance revealing trade name

indicators.note: getting round means surrounding, so the musicians enclose the resistance letter

parts.note: a group of musicians is a band
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A group of players overcomes opposition and shows off its label.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is the name or mark under which a company sells its goods.

clue.text: Scottish river's 150 years editor recalled

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the editor's letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A Scottish river has a history of 150 years, as an editor remembers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has' and is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Clyde is the river that flows through Glasgow in western Scotland.

clue.text: Breakfast food, much esteemed, light, leading couples used

indicators.note: leading couples asks for the front pair of letters from each of the following words

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal is highly prized and light, with front pairs put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading couples' takes two letters from the front of each word: MU, ES, LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Postpone introducing objective for back four player?

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something in, so the objective goes inside the postpone word

parts.note: to postpone is to defer
an objective is an end or aim

explanation.surface: Delaying the introduction of a goal for a football defensive line player.
explanation.walkthrough: In football (soccer) the back four is the line of four defensive players.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender is a footballer in the back line, often one of the back four.

clue.text: Shopper at first undecided, peers around, finding retail therapy?

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of shopper

parts.note: a matter undecided is still pending

indicators.note: around here means turned about, so the letters of peers are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper, hesitating at first, looks about and finds solace in buying things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like 'peers around' meaning looks about, but it signals a rearrangement; 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail therapy is jocular slang for shopping to cheer oneself up, often in a burst of extravagant buying.

clue.text: Part of the leg is theme for poet

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A portion of 'the leg' is the subject matter for a writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the poet; 'for' leads into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist is a poet who writes elegies, mournful verses for the dead.

clue.text: Relative from South is initially thorough, extremely rigorous

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the three words that follow it

explanation.surface: A relation from the south is, to begin with, thorough and very strict.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is a female sibling, a close family relative.

clue.text: Note I'd backed with some hesitation brings boredom

parts.note: TE is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: backed means reversed, so the letters of I'd run backwards

parts.note: I'd without its apostrophe gives the letters ID
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A message I had supported, delivered with hesitating ums, causes weariness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is the state of being bored by something dull and monotonous.

clue.text: Girl from Tenerife turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, so backwards
from says the letters are taken out of inside the word Tenerife

explanation.surface: A girl from the Canary island arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes ENERI from inside Tenerife and 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Musical term from southeast, good, usable — extremely

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of usable

explanation.surface: A musical expression from the southeast is good and very usable.
explanation.definitionFit: Segue is an Italian direction telling a performer to carry on into the next section without a break.

clue.text: Mark in German due, oddly selected

indicators.note: oddly selected picks the letters in odd positions, first, third and so on, of german due

explanation.surface: A score awarded in German is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade is a mark given for school work or an exam.

clue.text: Goods stolen from manipulated person after revolution

indicators.note: after revolution means once turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: someone used by others is their tool

explanation.surface: Stolen property taken from a dupe after an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is plunder, property taken by theft or in war.

clue.text: Fruit Twist left unfinished

indicators.note: left unfinished means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan, so Twist calls up his first name

explanation.surface: A cocktail's fruit garnish twist was abandoned half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like a verb or a cocktail garnish, but it stands for Oliver Twist; 'left unfinished' drops the last letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is the small oily fruit of the Mediterranean olive tree.

clue.text: Isle I'd learn about

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of I'd learn are moved around

explanation.surface: An island I would study.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is the large island west of Great Britain, so it is an isle.

clue.text: Weary about teetotaller, English — laughed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the weary word goes round the other letters

parts.note: weary means tired
TT is short for teetotal or a teetotaller

explanation.surface: Someone worn out laughed at the English abstainer.
explanation.definitionFit: To titter is to give a nervous, suppressed giggle, a form of laughter.

clue.text: Sounds like couple's type of fruit tree

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the word for couple is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a couple is a pair; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A twosome sounds like a kind of orchard tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear is a tree grown for its sweet, rounded fruit.
